title: Fix chat completion with outstanding tools
body:
## Summary

- keep eagerly started MCP and parallel tool promises owned by the Copilot prompt lifecycle even if their prompt children are flexed out
- wait for all request-scoped tool activity to settle before core chat marks an agent response complete
- make `blockOnResponse` observe both current and future terminal response states

## Root cause

This was both a tool-lifecycle ordering bug and a terminal-state observation race. Copilot could eagerly start an MCP tool but only await it if the corresponding `ToolResultElement` rendered, allowing prompt flexing to detach the running call. Core chat could then accept the model stop before request tools settled. Separately, `workbench.action.chat.open` installed its completion listener after receiving the response model without first checking whether it was already terminal.

The tool service now tracks settlement from before asynchronous validation/activation through invocation cleanup, and `ChatService` drains request tools before completing the response.

Refs microsoft/vscode-copilot-evaluation#6546

## Tests

- Copilot tool-calling tests, including delayed eager MCP completion
- Chat service lifecycle tests, including stop-before-tool-settlement ordering
- Chat action test for an already-complete response
- VS Code client and Copilot type checks
- targeted VS Code and Copilot lint

title: chat: do not notify when a session replays its history
body:
Opening a session that had already finished showed a "Session finished." OS
notification. Loading a session adds each historical request to the model and then
completes it, which is the same path that live work uses. The notifier saw that as
a response that had just finished.

- Notifies only when the last response of the session carries a completion time
  that is later than the moment this window started to watch the session. A
  replayed response keeps the completion time it originally had, or has none at
  all when that time was never recorded.
- Completes a streamed remote or agent host response with the current time when it
  finishes while the session is watched. That path shared the completion of
  replayed history, so a turn that finished under the eye of the user carried no
  completion time and could never notify. This also restores the completion time
  in the response footer for those turns.
- Derives that distinction from the completion state of the session: a session
  that is already complete when first observed finalizes replayed history, while a
  session that completes after it was seen running finished while watched.
- Removes the real timers from the notifier tests, which now take 10ms rather
  than 3s.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333250

Follow-up to #333038.

title: fix: guard disposed workspace in NES getDocumentByTextDocument (fixes #333555)
body:
### Summary Telemetry reports a `BugIndicatingError: Object disposed` thrown from `DisposableStore.assertNotDisposed()` in the Copilot Next Edit Suggestions (NES) inline completion path. The registered `InlineCompletionItemProvider` is invoked by VS Code core to resolve an in-flight completion request **after** the NES `VSCodeWorkspace` has already been disposed, so `getDocumentByTextDocument()` asserts on the disposed store and surfaces the error to telemetry. This is a use-after-dispose lifecycle race, not a logic bug: a disposed workspace legitimately tracks no documents. The fix returns `undefined` (the method's documented contract for untracked documents) when the store is disposed, before the assertion. Fixes microsoft/vscode#333555 Recommended reviewer: `@bryanchen-d` ### Culprit Commit Not identified — git history/blame is unavailable in this environment (blocked). The issue carries the `recent-regression` and `stable-anomaly` labels, indicating the assertion path began firing recently in the NES inline edits feature area (`extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/vscode-node/`). ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[VS Code core: resolve in-flight inline completion] --> B[InlineCompletionProviderImpl._provideInlineCompletionItems
inlineCompletionProvider.ts:287] B --> C[VSCodeWorkspace.getDocumentByTextDocument
vscodeWorkspace.ts:353] C --> D[this._store.assertNotDisposed
vscodeWorkspace.ts:354] D --> E{_store.isDisposed?} E -- yes --> F[onUnexpectedError BugIndicatingError Object disposed
lifecycle.ts:518] G[inlineEditsEnabled autorun re-runs
copilot token / quota change
inlineEditProviderFeature.ts:114] --> H[reader.store cleared -> VSCodeWorkspace.dispose
_store.dispose vscodeWorkspace.ts:174] H -.race.-> E ``` ### Affected Files - `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/vscode-node/parts/vscodeWorkspace.ts` — `getDocumentByTextDocument()` crash site (calls `_store.assertNotDisposed()`). - `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/vscode-node/inlineCompletionProvider.ts` — consumer that invokes `getDocumentByTextDocument()` from `_provideInlineCompletionItems`. - `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/vscode-node/inlineEditProviderFeature.ts` — producer of the disposal; the `inlineEditsEnabled` autorun clears its `reader.store`, disposing the workspace while the provider remains registered with VS Code core. ### Repro Steps 1. Enable Copilot NES inline edits so a `VSCodeWorkspace` is created and an `InlineCompletionItemProvider` is registered with VS Code core. 2. Trigger an inline completion request in an editor. 3. While the request is in flight, cause the `inlineEditsEnabled` autorun to re-run (e.g. a Copilot token/quota change) or deactivate the feature, disposing the workspace `_store`. 4. The queued completion resolves and calls `getDocumentByTextDocument()`, which asserts on the disposed store → `BugIndicatingError: Object disposed` in telemetry. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `vscodeWorkspace.ts`, `getDocumentByTextDocument()`: add an early `if (this._store.isDisposed) { return undefined; }` guard immediately before `this._store.assertNotDisposed()`. This aligns with the fix-the-lifecycle-race principle rather than masking symptoms: the provider is registered with VS Code core, which is a genuine external boundary that can legitimately call back after the workspace is torn down. The method already documents that it returns `undefined` for documents it does not track, and a disposed workspace tracks nothing — so returning `undefined` is contract-correct, not error-silencing. No `try/catch` is introduced, and no `logService.error`/telemetry call is removed; the assertion remains for the genuine in-lifetime misuse case where a disposed store is not expected. **Alternatives considered:** - Guard inside `_provideInlineCompletionItems` before calling `getDocumentByTextDocument` — rejected: it would duplicate the check at every one of the multiple call sites (lines 287 and 407) and leaves the shared method still throwing for other callers. - Wrap the call in `try/catch` — rejected: hides the disposal race behind swallowed exceptions instead of expressing the contract, and risks masking unrelated failures. ### Recommended Owner `@bryanchen-d` — current assignee of issue #333555 and maintainer of the Copilot NES inline edits area. No more specific CODEOWNERS entry exists for `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/`. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33408629224) · opus48 · 395.9 AIC · ⌖ 11.3 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: fix: clear stale data-index on dynamic-height measurement rows (fixes #333547)
body:
### Summary `unhandlederror-ListError [ProfileEditor-Tree] Invalid index 5` is thrown from `List.setFocus` in `listWidget.ts` when a user opens the context menu on a list/tree row. `setFocus` receives an index (`5`) that is `>= this.length` and throws `ListError Invalid index`. The index comes from `getItemIndexFromEventTarget` (`listView.ts`), which walks up from the pointer-event target reading the `data-index` DOM attribute. The value it reads is stale: it belongs to a transient **dynamic-height measurement row** that was appended to the live rows container without its `data-index` being refreshed. Because the measurement row is a cache-reused DOM node, it still carries the `data-index` from a previous render, which can point past the current list length. This bucket existed at low volume before 1.135.0 (2–3 hits) but spiked ~402x in stable 1.135.0 (804 users, 1627 hits), matching the introduction of batched dynamic-height measurement. Fixes microsoft/vscode#333547 Recommended reviewer: `@copeet` ### Culprit Commit `c2b336daae7101676f179b30f92641cdfcc6b38c` — "list: batch dynamic height measurements (#330967)" by Connor Peet (`@copeet`), authored 2026-08-18. Verified as an ancestor of the shipped commit `08d4889f9ec4a1685d257b9b95de036c8e1ce1e5` (1.135.0). This commit rewrote `_rerender` to batch dynamic-height measurements and introduced `probeDynamicHeights`, which allocates rows from the row cache and appends them directly into `rowsContainer` for offscreen measurement. Prior to this change, rows only entered the live container through `insertItemInDOM` → `updateItemInDOM`, which always sets a correct `data-index`. ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[User opens context menu on a row] --> B[MouseController.onContextMenu
listWidget.ts] B --> C[getItemIndexFromEventTarget
listView.ts:1541] C --> D[Reads data-index from DOM row] D --> E{Row is a transient
measurement row?} E -->|Yes| F[Stale data-index from
cache-reused DOM node
index >= length] F --> G[list.setFocus index
listWidget.ts] G --> H[List.setFocus throws
ListError Invalid index 5] subgraph Producer c2b336daae7 / PR 330967 P1[_rerender -> probeDynamicHeights
listView.ts:1786] --> P2[cache.alloc reuses released
DOM node with old data-index] P2 --> P3[rowsContainer.appendChild
without updateItemInDOM] end P3 -.stale attribute on live node.-> D ``` ### Affected Files - `src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listView.ts` — `probeDynamicHeights` appends measurement rows into the live `rowsContainer` (line ~1786-1792) without clearing/refreshing `data-index`. This is the producer of the stale attribute. `getItemIndexFromEventTarget` (line ~1541) is the reader that surfaces the stale value. - `src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/rowCache.ts` — `alloc` returns previously released DOM nodes which retain their old attributes, including `data-index`. - `src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listWidget.ts` — crash site only; `setFocus` correctly rejects the out-of-range index. Not modified. ### Repro Steps 1. Open a view backed by a dynamic-height list/tree (e.g. the Profiles editor, "ProfileEditor-Tree"). 2. Cause a re-render that triggers offscreen dynamic-height measurement so a cache-reused row is appended to the rows container while it still carries an old `data-index` that exceeds the current list length. 3. Right-click (open the context menu) such that the pointer event resolves to that transient measurement row. 4. `getItemIndexFromEventTarget` returns the stale out-of-range index and `List.setFocus` throws `ListError [ProfileEditor-Tree] Invalid index`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listView.ts`, in `probeDynamicHeights`: before appending a freshly allocated measurement row into the live `rowsContainer`, call `row.domNode.removeAttribute('data-index')`. This fixes the bug at the data producer, not at the crash site. The measurement row is a purely transient element used only for offscreen height measurement; it never passes through `updateItemInDOM`, so it never receives a valid `data-index`. When the row cache reuses a previously released DOM node, that node still carries the `data-index` from an earlier render, which can be `>= this.length`. title: fix: treat terminal disposal during run_in_terminal as cancellation (fixes #333549)
body:
### Summary

`run_in_terminal` (the terminal chat agent tool) throws a plain `Error('The terminal was closed')` when the terminal instance is disposed while a command is in progress (or was already disposed at strategy entry). Terminal disposal mid-command is an **expected** lifecycle event (the user closed the terminal, or the process exited), but a plain `Error` propagates up through `RunInTerminalTool.invoke` and is re-thrown as an `unexpectedException`, which reaches the global unhandled-error telemetry pipeline (`onUnexpectedError`). This produces the `unhandlederror-The terminal was closed` bucket.

The fix makes the producer throw `CancellationError` — the codebase idiom for an expected abort — which `onUnexpectedError` filters out via `isCancellationError`, and which the caller already maps to `error='canceled'`.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#333549
Recommended reviewer: `@Tyriar`

### Culprit Commit

`b537b64aa360` — "Handle terminal exit while terminal tool is in progress, Fixes \#264565" by `@Tyriar` (Daniel Imms), 2025-10-24.

This commit introduced the `onDisposed` race handling in both `richExecuteStrategy.ts` and `basicExecuteStrategy.ts`, and in doing so added the `throw new Error('The terminal was closed')` statements at both the strategy-entry disposal check and the post-race disposal branch.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[RichExecuteStrategy.execute] -->|instance disposed at entry / disposal race wins| B[throw Error 'The terminal was closed']
    B --> C[RunInTerminalTool.start]
    C --> D[RunInTerminalTool.invoke catch e]
    D -->|e not instanceof CancellationError| E[error = 'unexpectedException'; rethrow]
    E --> F[LanguageModelToolsService.invokeTool]
    F --> G[onUnexpectedError]
    G -->|not isCancellationError| H[Unhandled error telemetry bucket]
```

After the fix, the producer throws `CancellationError`, so at step D `e instanceof CancellationError` is true → `error='canceled'`, and `onUnexpectedError` filters it via `isCancellationError` before it can reach telemetry.

### Affected Files

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/richExecuteStrategy.ts` — 2 throw sites (strategy-entry disposal check, post-race disposal branch).
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/basicExecuteStrategy.ts` — 2 throw sites (same two positions).
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/browser/richExecuteStrategy.test.ts` — test updated to assert `isCancellationError`.
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/browser/basicExecuteStrategy.test.ts` — test updated to assert `isCancellationError`.

### Repro Steps

1. Ask Copilot to run a shell command via the `run_in_terminal` tool.
2. While the command is executing, close the terminal (or have the shell process exit) so the terminal instance is disposed mid-command.
3. The disposal race resolves and the strategy throws `Error('The terminal was closed')`.
4. `RunInTerminalTool.invoke` re-throws it as `unexpectedException`, and it surfaces in unhandled-error telemetry as `unhandlederror-The terminal was closed`.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** (both strategy files): replace `throw new Error('The terminal was closed')` with `throw new CancellationError()` at each disposal site. This fixes the error at the data producer, not the crash site: terminal disposal mid-command is an expected cancellation, not an exceptional condition. `CancellationError` (message/name `'Canceled'`) is the codebase idiom for expected aborts. The immediate caller `RunInTerminalTool.invoke` already contains `e instanceof CancellationError ? 'canceled' : 'unexpectedException'`, so the cancellation flows through cleanly as `error='canceled'`, and the global `onUnexpectedError` handler already filters `CancellationError` via `isCancellationError`, so it never reaches telemetry. Both strategy files already import `CancellationError` and use it directly below these sites for token-cancellation, so this aligns the disposal path with the existing cancellation path. The two test files were updated to assert `isCancellationError` on the rejection instead of matching the removed message string.

After this change, `richExecuteStrategy.ts` and `basicExecuteStrategy.ts` cannot produce an `unexpectedException` on terminal disposal because the thrown value is now a `CancellationError`, which both the caller and `onUnexpectedError` recognize and route as an expected cancellation rather than an unhandled error.

**Alternatives considered**:
- Wrapping the throw in a try/catch at the caller — rejected because it hides the error from telemetry instead of correctly classifying the expected event at the producer.
- Suppressing the message in `onUnexpectedError` — rejected because it special-cases a string in a global handler rather than fixing the producer's error type.

### Recommended Owner

`@Tyriar` (Daniel Imms) — author of the culprit commit `b537b64aa360` and owner of the terminal chat agent tools area.

title: fix: treat terminal disposal during run_in_terminal as cancellation (fixes #333549)
body:
### Summary

`run_in_terminal` (the terminal chat agent tool) throws a plain `Error('The terminal was closed')` when the terminal instance is disposed while a command is in progress (or was already disposed at strategy entry). Terminal disposal mid-command is an **expected** lifecycle event (the user closed the terminal, or the process exited), but a plain `Error` propagates up through `RunInTerminalTool.invoke` and is re-thrown as an `unexpectedException`, which reaches the global unhandled-error telemetry pipeline (`onUnexpectedError`). This produces the `unhandlederror-The terminal was closed` bucket.

The fix makes the producer throw `CancellationError` — the codebase idiom for an expected abort — which `onUnexpectedError` filters out via `isCancellationError`, and which the caller already maps to `error='canceled'`.

Fixes microsoft/vscode\#333549
Recommended reviewer: `@Tyriar`

### Culprit Commit

`b537b64aa360` — "Handle terminal exit while terminal tool is in progress, Fixes \#264565" by `@Tyriar` (Daniel Imms), 2025-10-24.

This commit introduced the `onDisposed` race handling in both `richExecuteStrategy.ts` and `basicExecuteStrategy.ts`, and in doing so added the `throw new Error('The terminal was closed')` statements at both the strategy-entry disposal check and the post-race disposal branch.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[RichExecuteStrategy.execute] -->|instance disposed at entry / disposal race wins| B[throw Error 'The terminal was closed']
    B --> C[RunInTerminalTool.start]
    C --> D[RunInTerminalTool.invoke catch e]
    D -->|e not instanceof CancellationError| E[error = 'unexpectedException'; rethrow]
    E --> F[LanguageModelToolsService.invokeTool]
    F --> G[onUnexpectedError]
    G -->|not isCancellationError| H[Unhandled error telemetry bucket]
```

After the fix, the producer throws `CancellationError`, so at step D `e instanceof CancellationError` is true → `error='canceled'`, and `onUnexpectedError` filters it via `isCancellationError` before it can reach telemetry.

### Affected Files

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/richExecuteStrategy.ts` — 2 throw sites (strategy-entry disposal check, post-race disposal branch).
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/basicExecuteStrategy.ts` — 2 throw sites (same two positions).
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/browser/richExecuteStrategy.test.ts` — test updated to assert `isCancellationError`.
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/browser/basicExecuteStrategy.test.ts` — test updated to assert `isCancellationError`.

### Repro Steps

1. Ask Copilot to run a shell command via the `run_in_terminal` tool.
2. While the command is executing, close the terminal (or have the shell process exit) so the terminal instance is disposed mid-command.
3. The disposal race resolves and the strategy throws `Error('The terminal was closed')`.
4. `RunInTerminalTool.invoke` re-throws it as `unexpectedException`, and it surfaces in unhandled-error telemetry as `unhandlederror-The terminal was closed`.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** (both strategy files): replace `throw new Error('The terminal was closed')` with `throw new CancellationError()` at each disposal site. This fixes the error at the data producer, not the crash site: terminal disposal mid-command is an expected cancellation, not an exceptional condition. `CancellationError` (message/name `'Canceled'`) is the codebase idiom for expected aborts. The immediate caller `RunInTerminalTool.invoke` already contains `e instanceof CancellationError ? 'canceled' : 'unexpectedException'`, so the cancellation flows through cleanly as `error='canceled'`, and the global `onUnexpectedError` handler already filters `CancellationError` via `isCancellationError`, so it never reaches telemetry. Both strategy files already import `CancellationError` and use it directly below these sites for token-cancellation, so this aligns the disposal path with the existing cancellation path. The two test files were updated to assert `isCancellationError` on the rejection instead of matching the removed message string.

After this change, `richExecuteStrategy.ts` and `basicExecuteStrategy.ts` cannot produce an `unexpectedException` on terminal disposal because the thrown value is now a `CancellationError`, which both the caller and `onUnexpectedError` recognize and route as an expected cancellation rather than an unhandled error.

**Alternatives considered**:
- Wrapping the throw in a try/catch at the caller — rejected because it hides the error from telemetry instead of correctly classifying the expected event at the producer.
- Suppressing the message in `onUnexpectedError` — rejected because it special-cases a string in a global handler rather than fixing the producer's error type.

`@Tyriar` (Daniel Imms) — author of the culprit commit `b537b64aa360` and owner of the terminal chat agent tools area.

title: Use setting for dictation cleanup model experiment
body:
## Problem

The dictation cleanup experiment and the Settings UI used two separate paths:

- ExP returned the legacy `dictationLlmCleanupModel` treatment.
- Settings exposed `dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel`, which continued to display `auto`.
- `ChatSpeechToTextService` separately read and cached the ExP treatment.

The experiment could change runtime behavior, but the visible setting did not reflect the effective model, making the experiment difficult to understand and verify.

## Fix

This PR makes `dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel` the single application-facing source of truth and removes the separate assignment-service lookup from `ChatSpeechToTextService`:

- ExP controls the setting default through the conventional `config.dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel` treatment name.
- `auto` follows the model supplied by that experimental default.
- An explicit user selection still overrides the experiment.
- The effective experimental model is available through the configuration system.

The ExP experiment must target `config.dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel`; the legacy `dictationLlmCleanupModel` treatment is no longer used.

This also updates automatic experiment refreshes to replace or remove their previous default. If ExP changes from Nano or Luna back to the control model, the old model no longer remains stuck. Experiment defaults are tracked per setting so refreshing one experiment does not disturb another.

## Testing

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --grep "ConfigurationDefaultOverridesContribution|ChatSpeechToTextService"` (13 passing per browser)

title: fix: cancel pending single-pane docked-tab reconciles on dispose (fixes #333537)
body:
### Summary The single-pane docked-tabs reconcile pipeline runs asynchronously on a `Sequencer`. When `SinglePaneDockedTabsCoordinator` is disposed (session switch / Existing-session strategy teardown / window close) while a reconcile is still queued or in-flight, that reconcile keeps running and eventually calls `IEditorGroup.replaceEditors`, which instantiates an editor pane through the coordinator's `IInstantiationService`. By then the DI tree has been disposed, so `createInstance` throws `InstantiationService has been disposed`. Impact: an unhandled error on the Agent Sessions window during teardown/session switching (Mac + Windows, 1.136 insiders). Fixes microsoft/vscode#333537 Recommended reviewer: `@sandy081` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`f45fb5350b9`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/f45fb5350b9) | | Author | `@sandy081` | | PR | #330573 | | Message | sessions: stabilize single pane lifecycle behavior | | Why | This commit introduced the `Sequencer`-based asynchronous reconcile pipeline (`queueReconcile` to `_reconcile` to `_reconcileCore`) with generation checkpoints, but `dispose()` was never overridden to cancel work already queued on the sequencer. A reconcile queued before disposal therefore survives teardown and reaches `replaceEditors`, which instantiates an editor pane through the disposed instantiation service. | > The reconcile pipeline has since been extended (e.g. #332365, "Show Changes view for new sessions", which added the `_reconcileForeignChangesEditors` to `replaceEditors` path seen in the stack), but the missing disposal cancellation is the underlying defect. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Trigger as Ambient trigger participant Queue as queueReconcile / Sequencer participant Reconcile as _reconcileCore participant Group as replaceEditors participant DI as InstantiationService Trigger->>Queue: queueReconcile(target, trigger) Note over Queue: reconcile queued on Sequencer Note over DI: Root cause: coordinator disposed,
DI tree torn down,
queued reconcile not cancelled Queue->>Reconcile: _reconcile(generation) runs after dispose Reconcile->>Group: _reconcileForeignChangesEditors then replaceEditors Group->>DI: createInstance(editor pane) Note over DI: Error thrown:
InstantiationService has been disposed ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/sessions/contrib/layout/browser/singlePane/singlePaneDockedTabsCoordinator.ts` | root cause / fix | L288-L297: `queueReconcile` queues `_reconcile(generation)` on `this._sequencer`; class had no `dispose()` override to cancel queued work | | `src/vs/sessions/contrib/layout/browser/singlePane/singlePaneDockedTabsCoordinator.ts` | crash path | L458-L478: `_reconcileForeignChangesEditors` calls `group.replaceEditors([{ replacement: this._instantiationService.createInstance(...) }])` | | `src/vs/workbench/browser/editor.ts` | crash site | L78 (from stack): `instantiate` to `createInstance` | | `src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiationService.ts` | throw site | L69 (from stack): `_throwIfDisposed` throws `InstantiationService has been disposed` | ### Repro Steps This is a teardown/dispose race, so it is timing-dependent: 1. Open the Agent Sessions window with a workspace-backed session that shows managed docked tabs (Changes + Files). 2. Trigger a reconcile (switch sessions, reveal the side pane, or open/close an editor) so a reconcile is queued on the sequencer. 3. Immediately dispose the coordinator before the queued reconcile resolves — e.g. switch away to a different session (Existing to New/QuickChat) or close the window while the async `replaceEditors`/`openEditor` step is pending. 4. The surviving reconcile reaches `replaceEditors` to `createInstance` on the disposed instantiation service and throws. To increase likelihood: rapidly switch sessions or close the window right after a session switch, which maximizes the window between "reconcile queued" and "reconcile reaches an editor-open call." ### How the Fix Works **Lifecycle pattern**: use-after-dispose. **Producer site**: `SinglePaneDockedTabsCoordinator.dispose()` (previously absent) — the disposable owner did not cancel callbacks already queued on `this._sequencer`. **Fix location**: `singlePaneDockedTabsCoordinator.ts` — new `dispose()` override plus entry guards in `_reconcile` / `_reconcileCore`. **Chosen approach** (producer-side; fix where the lifecycle is owned rather than guarding the crash site): - Added an `override dispose()` that bumps `this._generation` and clears `this._pending` before `super.dispose()`. Bumping the generation makes any reconcile still queued on the sequencer bail at its generation checkpoints, so it never proceeds to open/replace editors after teardown. - Added `this._store.isDisposed` to the early-return guard in `_reconcile`, and a `this._store.isDisposed` check immediately before the first async editor operation in `_reconcileCore` (`_reconcileForeignChangesEditors`), which is where the reported stack crashes. This covers a reconcile that was already past its entry check when disposal happened. body:
Cherry-pick of #333525 from `main`.

## Summary

Fix Automation runs that can remain permanently shown as **Working...** after legacy definitions migrate to Agent Host ownership.

The affected state is a non-terminal legacy run copied into the read-only history archive without a session resource. Once ownership changes, neither the legacy runner nor the Agent Host owns that archived run's remaining lifecycle. Besides producing a non-clickable history row, it permanently occupies the Automation's active-run slot.

## Changes

- Reject non-terminal run history before importing a legacy Automation into an Agent Host.
- Defer migration before any partial import while a source-owned run is active.
- Recover stale source runs before retrying provider migration, including providers registered after leader startup.
- Repair non-terminal archive rows from affected builds into deterministic terminal history.
- Persist repair with a dedicated compare-and-swap loop so stale repair cannot overwrite a newer terminal result.
- Distinguish active-run deferrals from genuine or mixed migration failures in logs and telemetry.
- Keep provider ownership transfers from moving while a run is active.
- Preserve optimistic conflict semantics and fully restore editable state when a run starts during transfer.

## Lifecycle guarantees

- A non-terminal run always remains with a component that can complete or recover it.
- The legacy archive contains terminal history only.
- Source data is removed only after destination state is durable and still matches the imported snapshot.
- Active authoritative Agent Host runs are never changed by legacy repair.
- Concurrent edits and terminal run updates win over stale migration or repair work.

## Validation

- 126 focused tests passed:
  - `agentHostAutomationStore`
  - `providerAutomationService`
  - `automationService`
  - `automationScheduler`
- ESLint passed for all changed TypeScript files.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

The cross-cutting Automations architecture specification will be submitted separately as a stacked documentation PR.

---

## Context

The Customizations modal has been redesigned with new UI and affordances. The redesign applies to both the regular VS Code workbench and the Agents window.

_Also see the end of this test plan for a suggested prompt you can give an agent to interactively guide you through this plan._

## Setup

- Install the latest VS Code Insiders
- Use a workspace with a mix of user and workspace customizations, including agents, skills, instructions, hooks, and prompts
- Configure at least one MCP server, one plugin, and an extension that contributes language model tools
- In the Agents window, create sessions for Copilot, Claude, and Codex harnesses
- Create or use a workspace with both kinds of migration candidates:
  - Deprecated user or workspace `*.prompt.md` files that can be converted to skills
  - Legacy User Data customizations that can be moved to a location supported by the active harness

## Overview and navigation

1. Open Customizations from the regular workbench and from the Agents window.
2. Verify the overview heading, introduction, cards, sidebar sections, item counts, and editor title describe the active customization target.
3. Navigate between the overview and each available section. Verify the selected section is retained, the correct search field receives focus, and back navigation from embedded detail pages works.
4. Switch between Copilot, Claude, and Codex harnesses in Agents window. Verify the modal title, project context, supported sections, overview cards, migration entries, and counts update together and do not show items from the previous harness.

## Agents, skills, instructions, hooks, and prompts

1. Inspect each available customization page and verify items are grouped under the correct source (such as workspace, user, remote, or built-in).
2. Search by name and description. Verify result counts, empty states, and source groups update correctly. Clearing search restores the full inventory.
3. Click on cards, rows, inline actions, and overflow menus. Verify actions apply only to the intended item and editable items open the correct source.

## Migration

1. Verify migration cards and sidebar counts appear only when the active workspace has eligible candidates.
2. Confirm per-item and per-group selection, including the checked, unchecked, and mixed group states.
3. Preview candidates, delete an unwanted candidate, and verify the destination and confirmation text are accurate.
4. Migrate a partial selection and verify selected files reach the intended destination without overwriting an existing target. Check that content formatting is preserved and unsupported metadata is called out for review.
5. Repeat while choosing to keep the original files.
6. Start a migration, switch the active Agents-window session before confirming, and verify the migration remains bound to the session and workspace where it began.

## MCP servers

1. Verify installed and marketplace sections load, search correctly, and distinguish installed, available, disabled, and plugin-owned servers.
2. Install an available server and open its embedded detail page. Verify source, scope, status, configuration or definition information, and back navigation.
3. Start, stop, and restart a server, then open its output and configuration. Verify status and available actions update without requiring the editor to be reopened.
4. Where available, verify setting-disabled and policy-disabled states explain why management is unavailable and do not offer actions that cannot succeed.

## Plugins

1. Verify installed, remote, recommended, and marketplace content appears in the appropriate sections.
2. Browse and search marketplace, then install a plugin and confirm it moves to the installed state.
3. Open installed and marketplace plugin details. Verify provenance, installation path and copy action, enablement or policy state, and the available install, update, enable, disable, and uninstall actions.
4. Inspect the plugin's contributed agents, skills, instructions, hooks, MCP servers, and commands. Open several contributions and verify navigation reaches the correct customization section or source file.
5. Install a plugin from source (such as the [Slack plugin](https://github.com/slackapi/slack-skills-plugin)) and create a plugin through the provided entry points.

## Tools and remaining sections

1. Verify tools are grouped by built-in, MCP or user-connected, and extension-contributed sources.
2. Expand tool sets, search for sets and individual tools, and exercise per-set and per-tool enablement.
3. Verify provider-owned or otherwise read-only sets cannot be changed and clearly communicate that state.
4. Browse extensions that contribute language model tools and verify extension management actions work in both the regular workbench and the Agents window.

## Keyboard, accessibility, layout, and persistence

1. Complete the main flows using only the keyboard. Verify logical focus order and visible focus for the overview, sidebar, search fields, cards, rows, inline actions, overflow menus, checkboxes, and detail-page back buttons.
2. Verify cards and controls activate with the expected Enter or Space key and that focus returns predictably after navigation or an action.
3. With a screen reader enabled, verify controls have descriptive labels and search result counts and state changes are announced without duplicate announcements.
4. Resize the editor between narrow and wide layouts. Verify cards, badges, actions, text, and scrollable regions reflow without clipping, overlap, or inaccessible controls.
5. Check representative pages in light, dark, and high-contrast themes.
6. Reload the window and verify the selected section, active target, inventories, counts, enablement states, and detail navigation recover correctly.

## Coding agent test guide

Give the following prompt to a coding agent to have it guide you interactively through this test plan:

```text
Please help me complete the test plan described in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333535. Act as an interactive test facilitator, not as the tester: do not assume that a check passed, and do not implement or fix the feature while guiding me.

First, read the full test plan and organize its checks into a checklist. Then guide me through it in small, logical batches. For each batch:

1. Tell me any prerequisites and the exact actions I should take.
2. Clearly state what I should expect to observe.
3. Wait for my verification before moving on.

You must use the Ask User Question tool after every batch so I can respond by clicking one of these options:

- It worked
- I found a problem
- I am blocked

Do not ask me to report the result in plain chat text. If I select "I found a problem," use the Ask User Question tool again to collect what happened, the expected behavior, and any useful reproduction details before continuing. If I am blocked, help diagnose the blocker or adapt the remaining plan without marking the checks as passed. When a prerequisite or feature is unavailable, record the affected checks as skipped or blocked rather than silently omitting them.

Keep a running record of passed, failed, and blocked checks. Do not mark anything as passed without my explicit confirmation. At the end, use the Ask User Question tool to confirm that I am ready to finish, then provide GitHub-ready issue descriptions I can paste into each issue I create against the test plan, that include:

- A concise summary of the issue
- Reproduction steps and observed versus expected behavior for each failure
- Relevant environment details
```

title: Preserve pre-encoded characters in MCP HTTP request URLs
body:
Fixes #289129

## Problem

When an HTTP MCP server is configured with a URL that contains percent-encoded reserved characters in its path (for example AWS Bedrock AgentCore runtime ARNs, which encode `:` as `%3A` and `/` as `%2F`), the connection fails because requests are sent to the wrong path.

Root cause: the configured URL string is turned into a `URI` via `URI.parse(configuration.url)` in `McpServerLaunch.fromServerConfiguration`. `URI.parse` percent-decodes the path and query, so `runtime%2Fmy-runtime-id` becomes `runtime/my-runtime-id`, and the encoded slash is now indistinguishable from a real path separator. The network layer then serializes with `uri.toString(true)`, which cannot restore information that was already discarded at parse time.

Note the query-string half of the original report (`=` becoming `%3D`) was already fixed by #247241 (`fc5d4141f9b`) switching `.toString()` to `.toString(true)`. That change does not help the path case, because no `toString` variant can recover pre-decoded reserved characters.

## Fix

Carry the exact configured URL string on the HTTP launch alongside the parsed `URI`, and use it verbatim for the actual network requests. The parsed `uri` is still used for origin, auth discovery, and display, none of which are affected by path/query decoding.

- `McpServerTransportHTTP` (and its serialized form) gains an optional `url?: string`, carried through `toSerialized` / `fromSerialized`. Optional with a fallback so the many existing construction sites keep working unchanged.
- `fromServerConfiguration` and the native discovery adapter set `url` from the raw configured string.
- `McpHTTPHandle` sends requests to `this._launch.url ?? this._launch.uri.toString(true)` at the five network call sites (DELETE close, POST message, streamable backchannel GET, SSE GET, and the SSE endpoint `new URL(...)` base), and its request logs report the same value.
- The MCP allow/deny policy identity (`McpServer._identityFromLaunch`) and the agent-host configuration projection use the raw URL with the same fallback, so security decisions and forwarded config describe the exact request target rather than the decoded one.
- `McpServerLaunch.hash` excludes `url` from the trust nonce when it equals the legacy request URL (`uri.toString(true)`), so preserving the raw string does not invalidate existing `TrustedOnNonce` approvals. Only URLs whose pre-encoding actually changes the request target get a new nonce.

The OAuth client-secret storage key and consent bookkeeping in `mainThreadMcp.ts` are left keyed on `uri.toString(true)`: switching them changes stored-credential and consent key derivation (invalidating existing entries on upgrade) for no practical gain, since OAuth discovery is origin-based and unaffected by path encoding.

## Before / after

For a configured URL like `https://…/runtimes/arn%3Aaws%3A…%3Aruntime%2Fmy-runtime-id/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT`:

- Before: request goes to `…/runtimes/arn:aws:…:runtime/my-runtime-id/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT` (decoded, wrong path segments) and 404s.
- After: request goes to the exact configured URL, byte for byte.

## Tests

- `mcpTypes.test.ts`: asserts `fromServerConfiguration` preserves the raw `url` (including `%2F` / `%3A`), that the parsed `uri` drops the pre-encoding, and that the raw `url` survives the serialize / revive round trip. Adds two `McpServerLaunch.hash` cases: the nonce is unchanged when `url` matches the legacy request URL, and changes when the pre-encoding differs.
- `extHostMcp.test.ts`: a handle-level test stubs the network boundary (overriding the protected `_fetchInternal`) and asserts the initial POST is sent to the raw configured URL, plus a companion test that the handle falls back to `uri.toString(true)` when no raw `url` is present.

Ran the MCP suites locally (`mcpTypes`, `mcpRegistry`, `nativeMcpDiscoveryAdapters`, `extHostMcp`, `agentHostMcpServerSupport`), all passing, including the `mcpRegistry` trust-flow nonce tests that guard the approval behavior above.

title: Fix SelectionMatchFindAction to respect seedSearchStringFromSelection setting
body:
Fixes #300085

## Description

`editor.action.nextSelectionMatchFindAction` / `editor.action.previousSelectionMatchFindAction` (Find Next/Previous Selection, `Cmd+F3`/`Ctrl+F3` and their Shift variants) ignore the `editor.find.seedSearchStringFromSelection` setting.

`SelectionMatchFindAction.run()` in `src/vs/editor/contrib/find/browser/findController.ts` hardcodes:

```ts
const selectionSearchString = getSelectionSearchString(editor, 'single', false);
```

Passing `false` for `seedSearchStringFromNonEmptySelection` unconditionally enables the word-at-cursor fallback inside `getSelectionSearchString`, regardless of the setting. So with `editor.find.seedSearchStringFromSelection: "selection"`, pressing `Ctrl+F3` with the cursor sitting on/near a word but no active selection still overwrites the current search term with that word — the same behavior as `"always"`, even though `"selection"` is documented to only seed from an actual selection.

`StartFindAction` in the same file already derives both parameters correctly from the setting:

```ts
seedSearchStringFromSelection: editor.getOption(EditorOption.find).seedSearchStringFromSelection !== 'never' ? 'single' : 'none',
seedSearchStringFromNonEmptySelection: editor.getOption(EditorOption.find).seedSearchStringFromSelection === 'selection',
```

This PR makes `SelectionMatchFindAction.run()` follow the same logic: skip seeding entirely when the setting is `"never"`, and pass `seedSearchStringFromNonEmptySelection = true` when it's `"selection"` so an empty selection no longer falls back to the word at the cursor.

## Testing

Added `issue #300085: Find Next Selection respects seedSearchStringFromSelection: selection` to `src/vs/editor/contrib/find/test/browser/findController.test.ts`: selects a word, runs `NextSelectionMatchFindAction`, then moves the cursor onto a different word with no selection and runs the action again, asserting the search string is unchanged rather than replaced by the word at the new cursor position.

## Verification

I don't have Visual Studio's C++ build tools set up in this environment, so `npm ci` can't build the native modules needed for the full Electron test run, and I didn't want to burn a lot of time compiling the whole project just to execute one test through Playwright, per the guidance in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` to prefer the smallest targeted verification over a full build/test run when confident in a change.

What I did verify:
- `npx tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck` — no errors in either changed file (the only errors reported are pre-existing `Cannot find module 'electron'` ones caused by `--ignore-scripts`, unrelated to this change).
- Manual review confirming the fix mirrors `StartFindAction`'s already-shipped, already-tested derivation of `seedSearchStringFromSelection`/`seedSearchStringFromNonEmptySelection` from the same setting, in the same file.

I'm flagging this explicitly rather than claiming a full test run I didn't do.

title: charts.orange defaults to semi-transparent #EA5C0055 due to minimap.findMatchHighlight fallback
body:
### Bug Description

In `src/vs/platform/theme/common/colors/chartsColors.ts`, `charts.orange` is registered with a fallback to `minimapFindMatch`:

```typescript
export const chartsOrange = registerColor('charts.orange',
    minimapFindMatch,
    nls.localize('chartsOrange', "The orange color used in chart visualizations."));
```

In PR #283365 (resolving #237507, *"Reuse editor colors in the minimap"*), `minimapFindMatch` was updated to delegate to `editorFindMatchHighlight` (`editor.findMatchHighlightBackground`):

```typescript
export const minimapFindMatch = registerColor('minimap.findMatchHighlight',
    editorFindMatchHighlight,
    nls.localize('minimapFindMatchHighlight', 'Minimap marker color for find matches.'), true);
```

Because `editor.findMatchHighlightBackground` has a default value of `#EA5C0055` (~33% alpha to avoid obscuring underlying code in the editor buffer), any theme that does not explicitly define `charts.orange` (including *Dark Modern*, *Dark+*, *Light+*, and most third-party themes) receives a semi-transparent color for `charts.orange` (`--vscode-charts-orange: #ea5c0055`).

### Expected Behavior

Chart colors (`charts.red`, `charts.blue`, `charts.yellow`, `charts.green`, `charts.purple`, `charts.orange`) are intended for data visualizations, commit graphs, and chart lines where colors should default to 100% opaque.

`charts.orange` should default to an opaque orange color (e.g. `{ dark: '#cd861a', light: '#d18616', hcDark: '#ab5a00', hcLight: '#0f4a85' }` or a dedicated opaque token), matching how `charts.green` and `charts.purple` have explicit opaque default color objects.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open VS Code with a theme that does not define `charts.orange` explicitly (e.g. *Dark Modern* or *Dark+*).
2. Inspect the computed value of `--vscode-charts-orange` in a webview or test page.
3. Observe that `--vscode-charts-orange` resolves to `#ea5c0055` (~33% opacity) instead of an opaque orange.

body:
## Summary

Fix Automation runs that can remain permanently shown as **Working...** after legacy definitions migrate to Agent Host ownership.

The affected state is a non-terminal legacy run copied into the read-only history archive without a session resource. Once ownership changes, neither the legacy runner nor the Agent Host owns that archived run's remaining lifecycle. Besides producing a non-clickable history row, it permanently occupies the Automation's active-run slot.

## Changes

- Reject non-terminal run history before importing a legacy Automation into an Agent Host.
- Defer migration before any partial import while a source-owned run is active.
- Recover stale source runs before retrying provider migration, including providers registered after leader startup.
- Repair non-terminal archive rows from affected builds into deterministic terminal history.
- Persist repair with a dedicated compare-and-swap loop so stale repair cannot overwrite a newer terminal result.
- Distinguish active-run deferrals from genuine or mixed migration failures in logs and telemetry.
- Keep provider ownership transfers from moving while a run is active.
- Preserve optimistic conflict semantics and fully restore editable state when a run starts during transfer.

## Lifecycle guarantees

- A non-terminal run always remains with a component that can complete or recover it.
- The legacy archive contains terminal history only.
- Source data is removed only after destination state is durable and still matches the imported snapshot.
- Active authoritative Agent Host runs are never changed by legacy repair.
- Concurrent edits and terminal run updates win over stale migration or repair work.

## Validation

- 126 focused tests passed:
  - `agentHostAutomationStore`
  - `providerAutomationService`
  - `automationService`
  - `automationScheduler`
- ESLint passed for all changed TypeScript files.

title: Center full-width characters in two monospace cells
body:
Adds an opt-in rendering and wrapping mode that forces full-width graphemes (CJK, Hangul, full-width Latin/digits, emoji, …) to occupy **exactly two monospace cells**, with the glyph centered inside that fixed-width box, instead of relying on the font's natural advance width.

New setting: `editor.forceFullwidthCharacterWidth` (boolean, **default `false`**). It is additionally gated on `fontInfo.isMonospace`, and is skipped for any line containing RTL characters.

The approach and its trade-offs (fixed-width spans vs. letter-spacing, grapheme clustering, bidi handling) are documented in `src/vs/editor/test/common/viewLayout/fullwidth-character-centering.md`.

Touched surfaces: view line renderer, `viewLine` pixel-offset reading, `RangeUtil`, both line-breaks computers (monospace + DOM), view model wrapping settings, GPU renderer eligibility, sticky scroll, ghost text, diff editor view zones, accessible diff viewer, and rich screen reader content.

---

## Manual UI verification checklist

Boxes are ticked as each behavior is verified.

**Setup** — monospace font, `"editor.forceFullwidthCharacterWidth": true`, and a scratch file containing:

- [ ] Caret sits flush against the box edges, not the glyph edges — the centering space belongs to the character

title: Preserve pre-encoded characters in MCP HTTP request URLs
body:
## Problem

When an HTTP MCP server is configured with a URL that contains percent-encoded reserved characters in its path (for example AWS Bedrock AgentCore runtime ARNs, which encode `:` as `%3A` and `/` as `%2F`), the connection fails because requests are sent to the wrong path.

Root cause: the configured URL string is turned into a `URI` via `URI.parse(configuration.url)` in `McpServerLaunch.fromServerConfiguration`. `URI.parse` percent-decodes the path and query, so `runtime%2Fmy-runtime-id` becomes `runtime/my-runtime-id`, and the encoded slash is now indistinguishable from a real path separator. The network layer then serializes with `uri.toString(true)`, which cannot restore information that was already discarded at parse time.

Note the query-string half of the original report (`=` becoming `%3D`) was already fixed by `247241` (`fc5d4141f9b`) switching `.toString()` to `.toString(true)`. That change does not help the path case, because no `toString` variant can recover pre-decoded reserved characters.

## Fix

Carry the exact configured URL string on the HTTP launch alongside the parsed `URI`, and use it verbatim for the actual network requests. The parsed `uri` is still used for origin, auth discovery, and display, none of which are affected by path/query decoding.

- `McpServerTransportHTTP` (and its serialized form) gains an optional `url?: string`, carried through `toSerialized` / `fromSerialized`. Optional with a fallback so the many existing construction sites keep working unchanged.
- `fromServerConfiguration` and the native discovery adapter set `url` from the raw configured string.
- `McpHTTPHandle` sends requests to `this._launch.url ?? this._launch.uri.toString(true)` at the five network call sites (DELETE close, POST message, streamable backchannel GET, SSE GET, and the SSE endpoint `new URL(...)` base).

## Before / after

For a configured URL like `https://…/runtimes/arn%3Aaws%3A…%3Aruntime%2Fmy-runtime-id/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT`:

- Before: request goes to `…/runtimes/arn:aws:…:runtime/my-runtime-id/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT` (decoded, wrong path segments) and 404s.
- After: request goes to the exact configured URL, byte for byte.

## Tests

Added a unit test in `mcpTypes.test.ts` asserting that `fromServerConfiguration` preserves the raw `url` (including `%2F` / `%3A`) and that it survives the serialize / revive round trip. Ran the MCP suites locally (`mcpTypes`, `mcpRegistry`, `nativeMcpDiscoveryAdapters`, `mainThreadMcp`, `extHostMcp`), all passing.

<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

Currently the Test Explorer tree gives no indication of how many tests a node (project / namespace / class / folder) contains. Visual Studio's Test Explorer and ReSharper/Rider's Unit Test Explorer show an aggregate count on every node, e.g. `MyProject (109 tests)` > `Directory (10 tests)` > `SearchUsersByObjectIdsTests (5 tests)`.

**Use cases**
- Sanity-check test discovery: a drop from 109 to 87 tests after a refactor or config change is visible at a glance, without expanding and counting.
- Gauge suite size per area/class quickly.
- Parity for users moving between VS Code and Visual Studio / Rider.

**What exists today doesn't cover this**
- `testing.countBadge` is a single global number on the Activity Bar icon, and only counts tests that have results.
- The run summary (e.g. `2/2`) is per-run, not per-node.
- Test extensions can't reasonably work around it by baking counts into `TestItem` labels (breaks filtering/sorting, and every provider would have to reimplement it).

**Proposal**
An opt-in setting (e.g. `testing.showCounts`) that renders the descendant test-case count after each expandable node in the Test Explorer tree, similar to how the Search view shows match counts per file.

Related but different: #181094 (Activity Bar badge, shipped as `testing.countBadge`), #117890 (totals in run progress).

title: test: Speed up Electron unit tests in CI

labels.name: engineering
labels.description: VS Code - Build / issue tracking / etc.

body:
## Summary

Speeds up Electron unit tests that wait for animation frames by preventing the test renderer from being treated as a hidden background window in CI.

- disable renderer background throttling in the unit-test `BrowserWindow`
- show the window without activating it when running in CI
- preserve the existing hidden-window behavior for local test runs

On Windows, `backgroundThrottling: false` alone does not prevent Chromium from throttling `requestAnimationFrame` in a hidden window. In the sampled CI run, 11 frame-driven tests took 94.9 seconds in Electron versus 1.5 seconds in browser tests.

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- targeted hygiene for `test/unit/electron/index.js`
- targeted Electron tests under CI conditions: 24 passing in 2 seconds
- representative test improved from 19.3 seconds in CI logs to 0.3-0.4 seconds locally under CI conditions

Full `npm run hygiene` could not start on Windows because `build/gulpfile.hygiene.ts` resolved the repository path as `C:\C:\repos\...\remote\package.json`; the targeted hygiene check passed.
